quoteEligibleExactSpans: God himself is the standard then God's goodness follows
the problem of evil still confronts theists

supportMap.description: Dembski identifies God as the source of all being and purpose and says denying divine goodness is incoherent.
supportMap.anchor: God is the source of all being and purpose

supportMap.description: He argues that an objective moral standard cannot stand outside God and instead must derive from God.
supportMap.anchor: any such objective moral standard cannot reside outside God

supportMap.description: He concludes that, once God's existence is granted, God's goodness follows from God being the standard.
supportMap.anchor: God's goodness follows as a matter of definition

supportMap.description: He qualifies the conclusion by retaining evil as a psychological or existential problem for theists.
supportMap.anchor: instead as a psychological or existential one

boundaryJustification.startWhy: Event 1749 is the first indispensable premise, stating that God is the source of all being and purpose before the argument about goodness begins.
boundaryJustification.endWhy: Event 1779 completes the indispensable qualification that evil remains a psychological or existential problem despite the definitional conclusion.
boundaryJustification.removedPrefix: Events 1715-1748 are removed because they introduce the debate, criticize Hitchens's framing, and develop the broader good-versus-evil paradox rather than the assigned bridge.
boundaryJustification.removedSuffix: Events 1780-1815 are removed because they add a future-destruction-of-evil argument, trust discussion, and a later repetition of the standard claim after the required qualification is complete.

quoteEligibleExactSpans: atheist view are subjective and contingent

supportMap.description: Dembski states that atheistic values are subjective and contingent, arising as behavioral and emotional inclinations.
supportMap.anchor: atheist view are subjective and contingent

supportMap.description: He attributes those inclinations to evolved conditions of survival and reproduction together with social upbringing.
supportMap.anchor: conditions of survival and reproduction under which our ancestors evolved

supportMap.description: He invokes the evolutionary account that morality is an illusion whose effectiveness depends on seeming objectively referential.
supportMap.anchor: in as much as it persuades us that it has an objective reference

supportMap.description: He contrasts Hitchens's community and the mutilation-practicing community as material groups inclined toward opposed behaviors.
supportMap.anchor: one group of material objects Enlightenment rationalists like Christopher Hitchens

supportMap.description: He concludes that atheism supplies no basis for objective morality although atheistic moral judgments act as if it does.
supportMap.anchor: The Atheist by contrast has no such basis for Morality

boundaryJustification.startWhy: Event 1857 begins the first indispensable claim that values on atheism are subjective and contingent, immediately followed by the evolutionary and social explanation.
boundaryJustification.endWhy: Event 1938 completes the specific conclusion that atheistic moral judgment acts as though it has an objective reference when, on this argument, it does not.
boundaryJustification.removedPrefix: Events 1826-1856 are removed because they frame the problem of good, quote Ingersoll and Dawkins, and include a personal aside before the assigned conditioning claim starts.
boundaryJustification.removedSuffix: No assigned-source suffix is removed: event 1938 is the original endpoint and is needed to finish the sentence denying objective reference to atheistic moral judgment.

repairs.longerCompleteArgumentRationale: Events 1857-1863 supply the evolutionary and social-conditioning explanation; events 1886-1907 supply the separated adaptive-illusion and objective-reference premise; events 1908-1922 supply the opposed-community material-disposition comparison; and events 1926-1938 supply the qualification and final conclusion. Retaining the intervening events is necessary because the required components are separated within one continuous argument and cannot be stitched.

limitations: The assigned source is an automatic-caption extract and contains apparent transcription errors and overlapping caption phrasing; no evidence outside this assigned source was consulted.
